question.text: When a Cat III AIF holds an unlisted debt instrument for which there is NO ascertainable market, valuation is done at:

answer.text: Amortised cost plus interest accrued from the date of purchase
DCF of all future cash flows at the risk-free rate
Last quoted price at the time of purchase, frozen until maturity

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 14.10.1, 'For unlisted securities for which there is no ascertainable market, valuation will be done at amortized cost of such security, plus interest (if any) accrued from the date of such purchase.' Amortised cost spreads premium/discount-at-issue over life using effective interest. The Trap: Face value ignores discount/premium. DCF at risk-free is a valuation technique not prescribed here. 'Frozen last quoted price' is a stale-price error. Cross-Exam Context: XV covers effective interest method. XIX-C applies to the specific AIF context where IPEV-DCF may also apply for distressed or non-performing debt. Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep an eye on credit events. The moment an unlisted debt shows stress (rating downgrade, missed interest), amortised cost is no longer appropriate — move to DCF with a stressed discount rate or collateral-based recovery valuation.
